memory_verse.text: "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God." — Matthew 5:9

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
E. Stanley Jones captured a profound paradox in Mahatma Gandhi: a man deeply rooted in his Hindu faith, yet so saturated with the Spirit of Christ that he "shamed" those who called themselves Christians. Gandhi didn’t just read the Sermon on the Mount; he allowed its "jewels" to reshape his very being. The world was moved not by his titles, but by the rare combination of candour and courtesy. He could speak the hard truth without losing his gentleness.
​We often claim the name of Christ but fail to mirror His character in the marketplace of life. If a man who drew his primary strength from the Gita could so perfectly illustrate the Cross, how much more should we, who claim the Vine, bear the Fruit? Our nation is not looking for more religious rhetoric; it is looking for the "living blend" of truth and love. We must bridge the gap between our silent meditations and our public actions. Let us no longer be content with admiring the "jewels" of the Sermon on the Mount, let us wear them in our daily conduct until our lives become a common center for a divided world.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "The soul of religions is one, but it is encased in a multitude of forms." — Mahatma Gandhi

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Heavenly Father, we thank You for the life of the Mahatma, who showed us that Truth and Love know no boundaries. Forgive us for the times we have kept Your Word in our books but not in our hearts. Grant us the courage to be candid yet courteous, and the strength to live out the Sermon on the Mount so that our lives may truly impact our nation. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: True influence doesn't come from shouting the loudest, but from living a life so aligned with Truth that people of all backgrounds find a common center in your character. Be the "living blend" today.
